Dear Dr. Jones
Re: Mrs. Patricia Welshman DOB: 28/03/1930

   Thank you for seeing Mrs. Welshman whose features are consistent with dementia and possible         Commented [OET1]: Unnecessary indentation
early stage of Alzheimer's disease.[space]Your full memory assessment for a definite diagnosis
would be highly appreciated.

  Today, Mrs. Welshman presented to me concerned about her memory issues.[space]She
reported forgetting hair dresser, dinner arragements and missing social events. She had some           Commented [OET2]: arrangements
issues with decision-making abilities and behavioural changes. On her mini-memory assessment,
she was found to have a poor short term memory and forgot to tell the day,[space]time and
month. space]Since she seemed to be suffering from Alzheimer's disease, I explained the diffrence      Commented [OET3]: difference
between Alzheimer's disease and its symptom[no space], dementia.

Please note[no space], [space]she has a family history of Alzheimer's disease and suffers from         Commented [OET4]: Mrs.Welshman: you should mention
osteoporosis.                                                                                          the patient name at the beginning of each paragraph


During her visits in last 8 months, she reported forgetting taking medications for her osteoporosis,   Commented [OET5]: Mrs. Welshman’s
elevated LDL and low vitamen D levels. Therefore, she was suggested to keep a webster pack with        Commented [OET6]: vitamin
her to ensure a good compliance with her medications. There was a history of fall in July 2014 for
which, an occupational therapist visit and community support care were arranged.

In light of the above, I have advised her a review consultation after your assessment. I would be
grateful if you could take over her care. Please, Ccontact me in case of any queries.


Yours sincerely,
Doctor.                                                                                                Commented [OET7]: no full stop

       use he/she.
   3. Your letter covered the case note with great simplicity and clarity.

       after it.
   5. Try to improve your punctuations further.

       therefore any British spelling words will be considered as a spelling mistake.
   7. Always proofread the letter.
